producer_report.summary: Added a behavior-evidence default to defaults.toml, applying to all work. Its first sentence is the core rule that criteria check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist. Later sentences require protection tests to show the action succeeding unprotected as the real user (root), then refused, and to fail rather than skip when the environment cannot enforce it. A unit test in defaults.rs checks the entry and its rendered line. Section 3.7 of defaults-loop.md has worked readings for 'make X read-only' and 'role calls a model'. CHANGELOG.md has an entry. I trimmed wording in reader.md, with no rule changed, to stay inside the reader token budget (1930).

checks_run.note: Full run exited 0 after the reader prompt was trimmed to fit the 1930-token reader budget.

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml has a new [[default]] entry (for example id "behavior-evidence") with applies_to ["*"], a source citing this request, and a statement whose FIRST sentence states the core rule (criteria check the requested behavior happening, not that types, files or wiring exist), because the rendered brief shows only the first sentence.
criteria_check.evidence: Read defaults.toml: entry behavior-evidence, applies_to ["*"], source cites the user request and this job id, first sentence is the core rule.

criteria_check.criterion: The statement's later sentences require that any protection/denial test first shows the action succeeds without the protection, under the same user and environment the real component runs as (root), then shows it is refused, and that if the environment cannot enforce the protection the test fails rather than skips or passes silently.
criteria_check.evidence: Statement sentences 2 and 3 in defaults.toml say exactly this; the unit test asserts the key phrases are present in the statement.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-data/src/defaults.rs parses the repository defaults.toml and asserts the new entry exists and its render() line appears with the core rule; run `cargo test -p athena-data` and see it pass, while existing tests (including root_cause_default_leads_with_the_core_rule) still pass.
criteria_check.evidence: Added behavior_evidence_default_leads_with_the_core_rule. The full cargo test --locked run passed, which includes athena-data and the root-cause test.

criteria_check.criterion: A worked example (docs/design/defaults-loop.md or a doc test fixture) shows a reading for 'make X read-only' whose criteria are: (1) a write to X as root succeeds before protection, (2) after protection the same write as root is refused, (3) the test fails, not skips, if the environment cannot enforce it (e.g. a root-bypassed file mode is not accepted as proof).
criteria_check.evidence: docs/design/defaults-loop.md §3.7 has the three criteria and names a file mode alone as unaccepted proof.

criteria_check.criterion: A second worked example for 'role calls a model' has criteria that run the role end to end and check the model call is made and its output is used (for example through the fake client, with the request observed), not merely that a client type or config is wired in.
criteria_check.evidence: §3.7 second example: runs the role against the fake client, observes the request, checks the reply is in the result; wiring-only forms are listed as rejected.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass from the repository root.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo fmt --all --check; all succeeded.

open_issues: briefs.rs was listed as an expected deliverable but needed no change; it is unchanged.

I did not add a protection sentence to reader.md because the reader token budget has no headroom; the rule reaches the reader through the rendered default's first sentence only. The detail sentences reach the producer and verifier through the full statement.
mistakes: My first edit shortened a governance sentence in reader.md and broke a lib.rs test; I restored the exact wording.
My first draft of the default's source text claimed a cause for the request that I had not verified; I replaced it with a neutral citation of the user request.
learnings: The reader token budget (1930, ceil(bytes/3)) in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs includes the rendered defaults, so each added default needs removals from the reader prompt.

crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs has a test that requires the exact phrases in reader.md about governance files ('Check whether the outcome needs a change to athena.toml, defaults.toml' and 'list that file as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion'), so these lines cannot be reworded.
desires: Rendered defaults count against the reader token budget, which a new default had to pay for; a budget report showing the current headroom would have saved three test runs.
